related_questions.question: What vaccines do I need to go to India?

text_blocks.snippet: While no vaccines are mandatory for travel to India, several are highly recommended to protect against common diseases. These include Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, Typhoid, and Polio. Depending on your specific travel plans, your doctor may also recommend vaccines for Japanese Encephalitis, Rabies, and Cholera. Additionally, staying up-to-date on routine vaccinations like measles, mumps, rubella (MMR), and tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis (Tdap) is crucial.
snippet_highlighted_words: Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, Typhoid, and Polio

list.snippet: Hepatitis A: Food and waterborne illness, highly recommended.
Hepatitis B: Transmitted through blood and bodily fluids, potentially from sexual activity, drug use, or medical procedures.
Typhoid: Transmitted through contaminated food and water.
Polio: May be required if arriving from a country with active transmission, and recommended for some travelers.
Japanese Encephalitis: Mosquito-borne disease, recommended for some travelers.
Rabies: Especially for travelers at high risk, such as those visiting rural areas or interacting with animals.
Cholera: Food and waterborne illness, recommended for some travelers.
Measles, Mumps, Rubella (MMR): Always recommended to be up-to-date.
Tetanus, Diphtheria, Pertussis (Tdap): Also recommended to be up-to-date.

list.title: Yellow Fever:
list.snippet: Vaccination may be required if traveling from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

list.title: Malaria:
list.snippet: Consider malaria prophylaxis (medication) depending on your travel itinerary and destination.

list.title: Influenza and Pneumococcal:
list.snippet: May be recommended for older adults or those with certain medical conditions.

list.title: COVID-19:
list.snippet: Check for the latest entry requirements, as regulations can change.
Consult with your doctor or a travel clinic to discuss your specific travel plans and determine which vaccines are appropriate for you.
Ensure you have any necessary certificates of vaccination.
Be aware of potential health risks and take necessary precautions like drinking purified water, using insect repellent, and practicing good hygiene.

text_blocks.snippet: India offers a range of COVID-19 vaccines for its citizens. As of July 18, 2025, the following vaccines are approved and widely available:

list.snippet: Covishield (Oxford-AstraZeneca)
Covaxin (Bharat Biotech)
Sputnik V
Moderna
Johnson & Johnson
ZyCoV-D

text_blocks.snippet: India launched its nationwide COVID-19 vaccination program on January 16, 2021. The government has implemented a centralized policy to ensure equitable access to vaccines.

Some of the vaccines, such as Covishield and Sputnik V, are manufactured in India under license from international companies. Others, like Covaxin and ZyCoV-D, are developed and produced domestically.

list.snippet: India has administered over 2.2 billion doses of COVID-19 vaccines as of March 4, 2023.
The government continues to encourage vaccination and booster shots to protect against COVID-19.
For more information on availability, registration, and vaccination centers, please visit the official website of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, India.

text_blocks.snippet: Note: This information is based on publicly available sources and may vary depending on the specific location within India. It is recommended to consult local authorities for the most up-to-date information.
